newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chirac backs early Czech EU, NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Chirac backs early Czech EU, NATO membership.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac pledged on Wednesday his support for Czech membership of the European Union in 2000, and of NATO a year earlier.

"I was able to confirm to the president that France unreservedly supports both the candidacy of the Czech Republic for the European Union, of which I think and hope it will be a member in the year 2000, and of NATO," he told journalists after talks with Czech President Vaclav Havel.
The Czech Republic is one of the leading candidates to be invited to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation at a July summit of the alliance in Madrid.

Chirac, on the first day of a two-day state visit, said France wanted a declaration approved on the candidacy of the Czech Republic, Poland, and Hungary, at the Madrid summit "so that they can truly be integrated in 1999".
"We want, moreover, that Romania be part of this first group, and I know that the Czech Republic has no objections to this," Chirac added.
Chirac previously has made similar statements of support for EU membership in 2000 during visits to Warsaw and Budapest, and backed Romania's inclusion in NATO during a recent visit to Bucharest.
